analysis.title: GS Pasi - Global Views Downside Growth Risks 26 Oct 2026
key_insights: World and G3 growth are tracking potential in 2026. Fiscal easing and the AI boom offset the Iran war and US tariffs. GS expects more of the same in 2027, with risks to the downside.
Gasoline, diesel, jet fuel and European/Asian gas are near or above their March/April highs on Middle East escalation fears.
DM long-end yields are up about 100bp since early 2026. If sustained, this costs a cumulative 0.6% of GDP. Only part of that is in GS forecasts, because GS expects fewer hikes than the market prices.

The AI investment impulse should peak in late 2026 or early 2027. The US wealth effect from AI stocks was worth about 0.4pp of growth over the past year and could fade sharply if AI stocks keep falling.
Firm-level AI adoption is now significantly correlated with weaker employment growth and higher unemployment outside tech.
An Oct 28 Fed hike is effectively ruled out. GS expects a 25bp hike to 4-4.25% on Dec 9, with a March hike possible if inflation surprises, and cuts in late 2027 or early 2028.
GS Fed scenario odds: 50% two hikes then cuts (baseline), 35% three hikes, 15% recession.
GS expects an ECB hold next week and a final hike to 2.75% in December. French bond turbulence could shave ¼-½pp from annualized growth and is a risk to the December hike.
GS expects the BoE to hike 25bp to 4% on Nov 5. Hikes are also expected in Canada and NZ this week and in Australia next week.

GS raised its 2026 China GDP forecast to 4.6% on Q3, but property, FAI and retail are weak. Hitting the target relies on a rising trade surplus (already 1% of global GDP), which raises the risk of trade barriers.

GS trade views: central banks will hike less than priced (strongest view); wary of momentum in equities but expects the S&P 500 to resume its climb after the midterms; cautious on IG tech with scope for a near-term HY bounce; JPY as a hedge against AI jitters; long oil products and European gas as escalation hedges.
